summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of type II diabetes, chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and morbid obesity was admitted for bilateral diabetic foot ulcers and peripheral edema. He underwent debridement of the ulcers in the emergency department and was started on oral antibiotics. During the hospitalization, he was evaluated for a vitreous hemorrhage in the left eye, diagnosed via ophthalmology consult, and prescribed eye drops with close outpatient follow-up. He received one dose of IV furosemide for fluid overload and was counseled on compression and wound care. His diabetes and anticoagulation were managed with home medications. He was discharged home the following day with instructions to continue wound care, complete antibiotics, monitor daily weights, and follow up with podiatry, cardiology, ophthalmology, and primary care.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Ulcer of other part of foot
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
